Check eligibility Trametinib for canine oral squamous cell carcinoma Cornell University · USA Location Cornell University Hospital for Animals, 930 Campus Rd, Ithaca, NY 14853 Study details Current / recruiting What is being offered: Dogs seen by Cornell University Hospital for Animals with diagnosed oral SCC are eligible for prescreen. Daily oral trametinib with scheduled follow-up through day 126. Cornell's live Clinical Trials roster and live contact form both currently offer this study. Who may qualify: Confirmed cancer diagnosis required; Active tumor required Costs / coverage: 🟢 Fully funded. All study visits, procedures and trametinib are free; dogs completing the study also receive a $1,000 credit toward standard-of-care SCC medical expenses. Contact: PI Santiago Peralta, DVM, AVDC, FF-AVDC-OMFS; Cornell Dentistry/Oral Surgery or Oncology/Clinical Trials Coordinator, 607-253-3060; vet-research@cornell.edu Official study / enrollment information → Combinatorial PDL1-IRDye800 imaging to guide surgery for canine oral cancer UC Davis Veterinary Center for Clinical Trials · USA Location UC Davis Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital, 1 Garrod Dr, Davis, CA 95616 Study details Active - Recruiting What is being offered: Protocol VCCT-26-008 enrolls dogs over one year old with confirmed oral SCC or oral malignant melanoma that are healthy enough for anesthesia and repeated visits. Anti-PDL1-IRDye800 is administered IV twice before near-infrared imaging at 8, 24 and 48 hours and repeat biopsy or curative-intent surgery. Published study period: July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028. Enrollment ends June 30, 2028.
